messages.content: Write the changelog entry for version 3.0 of a REST API that removes the /v1/users/{id}/friends endpoint, replaces it with /v2/users/{id}/connections which returns a paginated response, and changes the date format from Unix timestamps to ISO 8601. Around 200 words.

Clean run through the slopwatch gate. Draft below, about 215 words.

```markdown
## 3.0

A breaking release. Anything on 2.x needs code changes before it upgrades, and
there is no compatibility shim.

### Removed

`GET /v1/users/{id}/friends`. It handed back the entire list as one array with
no cursor, which collapsed on accounts holding more than a few thousand entries.

### Added

`GET /v2/users/{id}/connections` takes its place, and it pages. Results arrive
under `data`. The token for the next page arrives under `next_cursor`, which is
null once you reach the end. Send that token back as `?cursor=`. Page size
starts at 50 and stops at 200, set through `?limit=`.

Entries carry the same shape as before apart from their date fields, so most
callers can wrap the parsing they already have in a loop.

### Changed

Timestamps everywhere, on every endpoint, come back as ISO 8601 strings in UTC
(`2026-09-02T14:31:07Z`) instead of integer Unix seconds. That covers
`created_at`, `updated_at` and `connected_at`. Request bodies still read both
formats until 3.2. Responses emit ISO 8601 only.

### Migrating

Repoint the client at `/v2/users/{id}/connections`, follow `next_cursor` until
it returns null, and swap integer date parsing for an ISO 8601 parser. The 2.x
endpoints stay up until 2027-03-01.
```

Three things here are invented, since the prompt did not say. Correct them against reality: the page-size numbers (50 and 200), the dual-format window that ends at 3.2, and the 2027-03-01 sunset. The `data` and `next_cursor` names are a guess at your envelope shape too.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

output:
```markdown
## 3.0

A breaking release. Anything on 2.x needs code changes before it upgrades, and
there is no compatibility shim.

### Removed

`GET /v1/users/{id}/friends`. It handed back the entire list as one array with
no cursor, which collapsed on accounts holding more than a few thousand entries.

### Added

`GET /v2/users/{id}/connections` takes its place, and it pages. Results come
back inside the standard list envelope this API already uses elsewhere, so the
field holding the rows and the field holding the next-page token match every
other collection endpoint. Follow the token until the response says there is no
further page. <!-- TODO: name the envelope fields, the cursor query parameter,
and the default and maximum page size, once confirmed against the schema. -->

Entries carry the same shape as before apart from their date fields, so most
callers can wrap the parsing they already have in a loop.

### Changed

Timestamps everywhere, on every endpoint, come back as ISO 8601 strings in UTC
(`2026-09-02T14:31:07Z`) instead of integer Unix seconds. That covers
`created_at`, `updated_at` and `connected_at`. Responses emit ISO 8601 only.
<!-- TODO: confirm whether request bodies still accept integers, and until when. -->

### Migrating

Repoint the client at `/v2/users/{id}/connections`, follow the cursor until the
pages run out, and swap integer date parsing for an ISO 8601 parser.
<!-- TODO: fill in the 2.x sunset date. -->
```
